issues.claim: Congress has so far declined to enact comprehensive federal preemption, including rejecting such provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
issues.issue: Minor imprecision in characterization. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act contained a moratorium on state AI enforcement (initially a 10-year moratorium, later narrowed to 5 years tied to BEAD funding), not a 'preemption' provision per se. The Senate voted 99-1 to strip the moratorium. Multiple authoritative sources (Center for American Progress, McDermott Will & Emery, Goodwin) distinguish between 'moratorium' and 'preemption' as related but legally distinct concepts. The report's phrasing 'rejecting such provisions' (referring to 'comprehensive federal preemption') conflates the two. The practical effect is similar, but the legal mechanism differs.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider revising to: 'Congress has so far declined to enact comprehensive federal preemption or moratoriums on state AI laws, including the Senate's 99-1 vote to strip a state AI enforcement moratorium from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act'
